rca of the issue: Root cause of prior packaging issue: original .gitignore had a trailing `.env.*` exclude rule that appeared AFTER the `!**/.env.example` whitelist. Because gitignore uses last-match-wins semantics, the trailing exclude un-whitelisted the hidden dotfile templates, so `.env.example` files were not tracked in git — users cloning the repo received only the visible `env.example` copies (introduced as an alias earlier) but not the hidden `.env.example` originals. Fix applied by main agent: moved ALL whitelist rules (`!env.example`, `!**/env.example`, `!.env.example`, `!**/.env.example`) to the END of the environment-files block (lines 100-103, after all excludes 87-97). Verification: `git ls-files` now lists all 4 template files as tracked; `git check-ignore backend/.env.example` and `frontend/.env.example` both exit 1 (not ignored); the hidden templates now show status `A` (added/staged) in `git status`. Real .env secret files still correctly ignored by `*.env`.
